question: A classroom model contains directed segments joining the points $A(1,2,-1)$ to $B(4,0,3)$ and $C(-2,5,1)$ to $D(1,3,5)$. Students are told that vectors may be shifted parallel to themselves without changing their identity. They compare the directed segments using their component forms, magnitudes and directions. They also examine the vectors obtained by reversing a directed segment and by choosing the same point as both the initial and terminal point.(a) Obtain $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$.(b) Verify that $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are equal vectors.(c) Obtain $\overrightarrow{BA}$ and establish its relationship with $\overrightarrow{CD}$.(d) Determine $\overrightarrow{AA}$ and explain its magnitude and direction.
explanation: (a)`\overrightarrow{AB}=(4-1)\hat{i}+(0-2)\hat{j}+[3-(-1)]\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AB}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}`Similarly,`\overrightarrow{CD}=[1-(-2)]\hat{i}+(3-5)\hat{j}+(5-1)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{CD}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}`(b)The corresponding components of $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are equal. Their magnitudes are also`|\overrightarrow{AB}|=|\overrightarrow{CD}|=\sqrt{3^2+(-2)^2+4^2}=\sqrt{29}`Thus, they have the same magnitude and direction. Therefore,`\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{CD}`(c)`\overrightarrow{BA}=(1-4)\hat{i}+(2-0)\hat{j}+(-1-3)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{BA}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}`Therefore,`\overrightarrow{BA}=-\overrightarrow{CD}`Hence, the vectors have equal magnitudes but opposite directions.(d)Since the initial and terminal points coincide,`\overrightarrow{AA}=(1-1)\hat{i}+(2-2)\hat{j}+[-1-(-1)]\hat{k}=\vec{0}`Its magnitude is $0$. A zero vector has no definite direction because all its components are zero.

options.A:
(a) $\overrightarrow{AB}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{CD}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$
(b) The vectors are unequal
(c) $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$
(d) $\overrightarrow{AA}=\vec{0}$ with magnitude $0$
options.D:
(a) $\overrightarrow{AB}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{CD}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$
(b) $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{CD}$
(c) $\overrightarrow{BA}=-\overrightarrow{CD}$
(d) $\overrightarrow{AA}=\vec{0}$, with magnitude $0$ and no definite direction
